texts.value: Flavoenzyme which catalyzes the oxidation of spermine to spermidine. Can also use N(1)-acetylspermine and spermidine as substrates, with different affinity depending on the isoform (isozyme) and on the experimental conditions. Plays an important role in the regulation of polyamine intracellular concentration and has the potential to act as a determinant of cellular sensitivity to the antitumor polyamine analogs. May contribute to beta-alanine production via aldehyde dehydrogenase conversion of 3-amino-propanal
Inhibited at more than 90% by SL-11144, SL-11150 and SL-11158, at concentrations less than 1 uM
kcat is 27-fold higher with spermine than N1-acetylspermine as substrate for isoform 1 and isoform 6.
Optimum pH is 9.5 with spermine as substrate.
Amine and polyamine degradation; spermine degradation
The resultant proteins have different biochemical characteristics and substrate specificity.
Widely expressed. Expressed in human tumor cell lines. Isoform 4 is only found in an embryonal kidney cell line
Major isoform. Has the highest affinity for the 3 substrates. Has a greater affinity for spermidine and spermine than for N(1)-acetylspermine
Has the lowest Km values for the different substrates and has the highest affinity for spermidine
Does not seem to display oxidase activity towards spermidine or N(1)-acetyl-spermine, but this has to be confirmed
Substrate specificities and affinities comparable to those of isoform 1
Belongs to the flavin monoamine oxidase family
